text: The Council plans to replace the Quillbeck housing records system during 2028, and the replacement has not yet been procured.
An internal audit in 2025 found duplicate resident records in about eight percent of the Quillbeck data, and a project to cleanse the data has not yet started.
Annual license renewals peak in January, when about forty percent of the year's licensing cases are opened.
Under the current support contract, the supplier must send monthly performance reports to the Council's audit committee.
The housing team moves to new offices at Tanner's Yard during August and September 2027.
The Council's annual window for penetration testing runs from 1 September to 30 September, and a test outside it needs the approval of the Chief Information Officer.
Tenders must be submitted through the Halverton e-Tendering Portal by 12:00 GMT on 2027-01-15, and the portal accepts no upload after that time.
Bidders may ask clarification questions through the portal until 12:00 GMT on 2026-12-18.
The Form of Tender must be signed by a director of the bidder and uploaded as a separate file, and a tender without it is rejected.
The quality response is one PDF file of at most 30 pages of A4, set in type of at least 11 points, and pages after the thirtieth are not read.
The quality response must not name the bidder, its staff, its subcontractors or its clients, so that evaluators can score it without knowing who wrote it.
The bidder must have had an average annual turnover of at least £4,000,000 over its last three financial years.
The bidder must hold ISO/IEC 27001 certification that covers the data centers and the support teams that deliver the service.
The service shall handle every case type the Council uses, including repairs, licensing applications, complaints, environmental health requests, etc.
The service meets the requirements listed in Annex B, which form part of this specification.
The service shall give field inspectors a mobile application that works without a network connection and stores each photograph with its GPS location.
Bidders may offer a chat assistant on the resident portal as an optional extra, priced separately in Annex C.
The service shall let authorized staff configure case types, stages, forms and service levels without any change to the software code.
The service shall send the resident an acknowledgment with a case reference within one working day of a case being opened.
The service shall provide appropriate response times for every case type, so that residents know when to expect an answer.
The Contractor is responsible for keeping every audit record for seven (7) years after the case closes.
The resident portal shall offer a video call with a British Sign Language interpreter during Service Hours.
The resident portal should let each resident choose to receive updates by e-mail or by text message.
Where a resident asks for a paper copy of a case decision, the Contractor sends it by post within five working days.
The service should let staff send a resident a secure link to pay a license fee online.
The Contractor shall provide at least 500 of document storage for each year of the contract.
The service shall support up to TBC concurrent named users at peak times.
The service shall produce the statutory returns in the formats set out in Schedule 7.
The service shall exchange tenancy, property and repair order data with the Quillbeck housing records system through its SOAP web service, within five minutes of each change.
The supplier of the Quillbeck system shall give the Contractor access to a test copy of its SOAP web service for the whole implementation.
The Contractor shall migrate all 1.2 million historic case records and their documents from the current systems by 2027-12-31, with no record lost.
Bidders may propose an alternative to the file export of the Thornlea document archive if it moves every document with its metadata.
Connections between the service and the Council's network shall run over the Halverton Public Services Network, with its current accreditation in place.
The Contractor shall host the service in data centers in the United Kingdom and shall keep a disaster recovery site at least 50 kilometers from the primary site.
The Contractor shall commission an independent penetration test of the service before go-live and once a year after that.
The Contractor should publish its planned maintenance windows to the Council at least ten working days in advance.
The Council reserves the right to inspect the Contractor's hosting and support sites on ten working days' notice.
Respond within 30 minutes and resolve within four hours.
Respond within one hour and resolve within one working day.
Where availability falls below 99.9% in a calendar month, the Contractor shall pay service credits of five percent of the monthly charge for each 0.1% below that target.
The service must be live for all four teams by 2027-10-01.
Bidders may propose a phased go-live, one team at a time, provided that every team is live by 2027-10-01.
The Contractor shall train all users before go-live.
The tender must name a delivery lead who stays in the role from the contract start until three months after go-live.

text: The Council will provide two members of each team to take part in user acceptance testing.
On termination for convenience, the Contractor shall continue the service for up to six months at the Council's request, at the prices then in force.
The Contractor should place at least a quarter of its subcontracted spend with small businesses based in the region.
"Service Hours" means 08:00 to 18:00 on Working Days, during which the Contractor's service desk answers calls from Council staff.
The Contractor shall accept unlimited liability for any loss of personal data caused by its breach of the contract.
The Contractor shall indemnify the Council against any claim by a third party that the service infringes a patent, copyright or trade mark.
All intellectual property rights in the configurations, reports and documents created for the Council are owned by the Council from the moment of their creation.
The Contractor shall process personal data only on the Council's documented instructions, as the Council's data processor.
The Contractor shall keep professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000 for six years after the contract ends.

Prices must be given in pounds sterling, excluding VAT, and stay fixed for the first three years of the contract.

The Quillbeck integration targets a system the Council replaces during 2028.
The January peak of license renewals arrives three months after go-live, while the service is still new.
Duplicate resident records in eight percent of the Quillbeck data meet a migration that may lose no record.
The September window for penetration tests leaves no time to fix findings before go-live on 2027-10-01.
The housing team moves offices in August and September 2027, when every user is to be trained.
